Answer: A
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates a distinct, curvilinear calcification along the inferior and posterior border of the cardiac silhouette, which is the classic radiographic appearance of a calcified left ventricular aneurysm. This finding typically represents a sequela of a prior myocardial infarction where the scarred ventricular wall has undergone dystrophic calcification.
